desc: Prove/verify the reduction: any good caption's blocks can be split into blocks of length 3–5, so DP with block lengths {3,4,5} suffices for both cost and lexicographic optimality.
Design segment cost helper: for segment caption[i:i+L] (L in {3,4,5}), minimal operations to make it uniform via median character (lower median for L=4), computed by sorting ≤5 elements.
Design DP: dp[i] = (min cost, best string) for suffix caption[i:], transitions over L in {3,4,5} from dp[i+L]; impossibility (n<3 or unreachable) returns "".

Design tie-breaking: among equal-cost transitions choose lexicographically smallest full string via (cost, string) tuple comparison; per segment use smallest optimal letter; sliding-window cleanup of stored strings to keep memory O(5n).

Implement the solution in the starter code: precompute segment (cost, letter) for L=3,4,5; right-to-left DP storing (cost, string) with sliding-window cleanup; store choice per position; reconstruct answer by walking choices from index 0.

Test against examples ("cdcd" → "cccc", "aca" → "aaa", "bc" → "") plus edge cases: n<3, already-good captions, all-same strings (worst-case performance with n=5e4), and random brute-force verification on small inputs.
